From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.inference.com>
To: Sam Park <sam.park@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.inference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.inference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: POC environment & access plan (IP allowlist / peering)

Sam —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. As discussed, I pulled together a concise Mutual Action Plan (v1) focused on the POC environment handoff and the immediate access items we need to close in order to start the evaluation next week. High-level ask: can we confirm owners and target dates for the items below by EOD tomorrow?

Summary checklist (POC activation):
- Org setup: create Acme Health org in Redwood Console + add 3 seats (owner: Acme) — target: 2026-07-01
- API keys: create scoped API key for evaluation (no production perms) — target: 2026-07-01
- IP allowlist: Acme to provide IP ranges (ingress) + Redwood to confirm endpoints — target: 2026-07-02
- VPC peering: exchange CIDR ranges and initiate peering request (template attached) — target: 2026-07-03
- Minimal test plan: 3 smoke tests (auth, sample generate, KV cache) — target: 2026-07-05

Notes / constraints:
- We will supply a limited-duration API key scoped to evaluation (rotated at close).
- If you require VPC peering, we need CIDR and contact for your network team.
- For SOC2 evidence requests, please send the questionnaire; Marcus will own the response.

I've attached a working MAP spreadsheet (MAP-Acme-POC-v2.xlsx) and a short VPC peering template (vpc-peering-template.txt) for your network team.

Next steps (suggested):
1) You confirm owner for org creation + who should receive the invite.
2) Share IP allowlist and network contact for peering.
3) Procurement — let me know if procurement needs a separate thread (they often ask for a statement of work and PO).

Thanks — aiming to have the environment live before your demo on 2026-07-06.

— Irene
Irene Choi
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks, Irene — this is helpful. A few quick answers and questions from our side.

- Owner for org creation will be me (sam.park@acmehealth.com). Please send the invite to that address.
- I attached our network lead (Miguel) here. Miguel: can you confirm CIDR ranges we can use and whether we prefer peering or transit?
- Procurement: cc'd procurement@acmehealth.com — they will need a one-page SOW and pricing summary (we can handle PO once SOW is approved).

Security question: our security team asked if Redwood supports short-lived API keys (or at least automatic rotation). Is that something you can accommodate for the POC?

Also — approximate expected egress IPs from Redwood so we can start firewall planning. If you can provide the endpoint hostnames + ranges that helps.

Appreciate this — target dates look reasonable but Miguel will confirm the peering timeline.

Best,
Sam
Product Lead, Acme Health

Irene / team — quick internal note on the technical pieces so we can answer Sam's questions.

- Short-lived keys: we can issue a key with an expiration (48h) for initial smoke runs and a second scoped key that lasts the full POC (rotated weekly on request). For evaluation convenience we'll provision a long-lived scoped key and a short-lived one for smoke.
- Egress IPs: Redwood's hosted endpoints are in 3 AZs in us-west2. For the POC we'll provide a small set of static egress prefixes (example: 34.82.12.0/24, 34.82.13.0/24). I'll confirm exact prefixes once our infra team signs off.
- VPC peering: use the template Irene attached. We require your VPC CIDR and a contact for BGP/peering ops. Peering typically completes within 24–48h once both sides accept the request.

I'll draft a short paragraph for procurement that outlines the POC scope + temporary credits. Irene, want me to add that to the MAP spreadsheet?

— Marcus
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks — Miguel here (network lead). A couple things from our side:

1) Preferred approach: VPC peering to avoid transit costs. We'll share CIDR ranges below.
2) CIDR ranges: 10.40.0.0/16 (primary), we can allocate a /24 for the peering if required.
3) Firewall: we need Redwood to provide the egress prefixes ASAP so we can open the allowlist.
4) Contact for peering setup: miguel@cloudops.co, +1-415-555-0199.

Procurement: procurement@acmehealth.com — I'll coordinate the SOW signoff timeline; we expect PO within 7–10 business days after SOW acceptance.

Let me know when you have the egress prefixes and the peering request.

Miguel
CloudOps — Acme Health

Miguel —

Thanks, that works. Confirming the temporary egress prefixes for the hosted POC endpoints (subject to final infra CIDR assignment):
- 34.82.12.0/24
- 34.82.13.0/24
- 34.82.14.0/24

If you can allow the three /24s for the POC, we should be good for initial traffic. Regarding peering, please complete the vpc-peering-template.txt with your VPC ID and desired peering CIDR (we'll initiate from our side once we have your entries).

API keys: we'll provide two keys as discussed (one short-lived for smoke, one scoped longer for the POC). Keys will be delivered via the Redwood Console invite and through a secure note in the MAP spreadsheet.

Irene — I'm dropping a short procurement blurb below that you can paste into the MAP for Acme procurement: 
- POC scope: hosted inference for up to 100k tokens/day, limited production-like tests, 30-day evaluation window, included support for peering and SOC2 questionnaire response. Temporary credits will apply as outlined in the MAP.

— Marcus
